summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and esophageal varices, was admitted after presenting with hematemesis and bloody stools. He was found to have a low hemoglobin and was transfused one unit of packed red blood cells. An endoscopy revealed a bleeding arteriovenous malformation in the antrum, which was successfully treated with argon plasma coagulation. His abdominal pain improved with tramadol, and his blood pressure was controlled by restarting lisinopril and continuing nadolol. He was monitored for alcohol withdrawal using the CIWA scale, which resolved without medication. The patient left the hospital against medical advice before a follow-up CBC was reviewed but was discharged on oral PPI, antihypertensives, and supportive medications with instructions to avoid alcohol and follow up with his primary and liver specialists.
problems: Angiodysplasia of stomach and duodenum with hemorrhage
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Esophageal varices in diseases classified elsewhere, without mention of bleeding
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, continuous
Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
